reason: This short historical vulnerability report supports two reusable observations: downstream document delivery needs its own identity gate, and reported visibility of non-owned records raises a separate object-authorization question. It corroborates existing library principles rather than supplying a new testing technique. The article names no research tools and provides no systematic controls or repair-validation evidence.

workflow.decision: Identify the downstream artifact-delivery boundary in an ordinary application workflow. Question whether its consumer enforces identity independently instead of assuming an earlier login stage protects every later delivery operation.

Keep identity establishment and object ownership as separate policy questions. Reported non-owned-record visibility warrants object-authorization review, but unspecified actor and session conditions must remain unresolved rather than being folded into a single proven mechanism.

handoffs.when: A workflow produces a protected artifact whose delivery boundary may not share the upstream identity or ownership gate.
packet: ordinary workflow stage and downstream delivery boundary
source-author observations and exact evidence locators
unknown gates, missing controls, and bounded next question
handoffs.acceptance_gate: Accept this article only as author-report-backed audit prioritization. Keep identity and ownership enforcement unresolved until authorized-artifact evidence supports each gate; reject packets containing non-owned data or asserting current exposure.

limitations: The report concerns a historical deployment; reading the blog does not establish present-day exposure. No target requests or reproduction were performed.

Absent session binding and non-owned-record visibility are author reports. The article does not document independent actor/session controls, backend policy decisions, source code, or a complete root-cause analysis.
The opening correction notice supplies no patch artifact, regression results, equivalent-route coverage, or deployed-enforcement evidence; repair remains an author claim.
The report includes real-team examples. Screenshot contents and personal or team identifiers were not extracted; no affected-record inventory or exposure magnitude is supported.

candidate_additions.guidance: Include generated-document delivery in the interface inventory. An authenticated navigation path is not evidence that a downstream artifact consumer enforces the same identity gate.

Record session requirements and object-ownership policy separately for artifact delivery. Preserve unknown actor/session conditions when a source reports both anonymous access and non-owned-record visibility without independent controls.
